constants.name: TA_ACTION_IN_TRANSITION
constants.doc: owner: a transition ID, initial transitions included

constants.name: TA_ACTION_IN_ELSE
constants.doc: owner: an <if > action; an <elseif > is an <if > here

ta_action_block.doc: The block of executable content an action sits in, and what `owner` is.

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: The element: raise, send, cancel, assign, script, log, if or foreach.

fields.name: owner
fields.doc: A state, transition or action ID, as `block` says.

fields.name: block_index
fields.doc: Which of the owner's blocks of that kind, from 0, in document order: the <onentry > or <onexit > element, or the <invoke > of FINALIZE; 0 for every other block.

fields.name: index
fields.doc: Its place in the block, from 0.

fields.name: service_handle
fields.doc: Runtime-only: session images do not retain or reconstruct this handle.

ta_actor_active_states_params.doc: The active configuration: every active state, ancestors included, in document order. Resolve IDs with ta_definition_state().

ta_actor_capture_params.doc:
A session image is an owned in-memory representation of Tinyactors-managed interpreter state.  It is not a persistence wire format and does not contain the host-owned data-model object graph.  Host values referenced by interpreter-owned events, timers, or continuation state are retained as host references according to ta_value lifetime rules.

Invoker service handles are runtime-only and are not rebound.  Restoring an image retires every invocation that was active in it and appends one `error.communication.invoke. <id >.unavailable` platform event to the internal queue.  The event name identifies the invocation; its invoke_id field remains TA_INVOKE_ID_NONE because the event was generated by the processor, not the invoked service.  Those events follow internal events already captured by the image.  An active invocation therefore does not make capture or restoration return TA_ERR_NOT_RECONSTRUCTIBLE.

ta_actor_reconstruct() restores an image without participating in named routing. ta_actor_load() wraps the same reconstruction in the named-actor residency protocol and publishes it only when the directory still says UNLOADED. An image is still the host's to hold, to index by ta_session_image_next_deadline(), and to destroy.

An unpublished prepared replacement is not a routable session yet and cannot be captured; ta_actor_capture() returns TA_ERR_BUSY until activation.

ta_actor_completion.doc: Release data with ta_value_release() when has_data is true.

fields.name: trace
fields.doc: What the macrostep that takes the event runs under (ADR 0067); a router passes ta_external_delivery.trace. All zero is none.

fields.name: actor
fields.doc: Meaningful only for TA_ACTOR_DIRECTORY_RESIDENT.

ta_actor_directory_vtable.doc: The directory is keyed by address handle (ADR 0065): equal addresses are the same pointer, so a directory can key its map by the pointer. The handle is borrowed for the call; a directory that keeps an entry retains the address (ta_address_retain) and releases it when the entry goes.

fields.name: claim
fields.doc: claim succeeds only when the address has no entry.

fields.name: replace
fields.doc: replace/remove are atomic comparisons against params->expected.

ta_actor_history_params.doc: The states recorded by one history pseudo-state, in document order. `*count` is zero when the history has never been recorded; its default transition then applies.

ta_actor_id.doc: A resident actor: its table slot in the low 32 bits and the slot's generation in the high 32 bits (ADR 0059). Zero is never a valid ID, and no slot is ever issued generation 0, so a host may use generation 0 for "no actor". When an actor goes away its slot's generation moves on, so its ID goes stale (TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND) and never names the slot's next occupant. Split and join IDs with ta_actor_id_slot(), ta_actor_id_generation() and ta_actor_id_make() rather than with bit arithmetic.

ta_actor_inspection.doc:
A read-only operational view of one resident interpreter instance.

Fixed-size facts are fields; the internal queue, the invocations and the delayed sends are borrowed arrays; the active configuration and history are read with the ta_actor_* list functions below, whose counts are reported here so a host can size buffers once. Inspecting one actor costs O(size of that actor), never O(size of the system) (ADR 0054).

Core pointers are borrowed and valid only while the actor is externally synchronized against mutation. The completion pointer and its data are borrowed and must not be released. Inspection never calls the data-model adapter; read the data model with ta_actor_datamodel_root().

fields.name: session_id
fields.doc: The SCXML session this actor holds, as _sessionid reads it (ADR 0066): the runtime ID the session was spawned with, kept across unload and load. It equals `actor` until the session has been reloaded.

fields.name: active_state_count
fields.doc: Number of states in the active configuration, ancestors included.

fields.name: macrostep_in_progress
fields.doc: True while a macrostep is paused mid-way (ta_actor_resume() continues it).

fields.name: microstep_in_progress
fields.doc: True while it is paused inside a microstep, in executable content (ADR 0061). The active states are then those after the last completed microstep.

fields.name: current_event
fields.doc: The external event of the paused macrostep, or null.

fields.name: delayed_sends
fields.doc: Pending delayed sends, ordered by due time, then send order.

fields.name: final_state
fields.doc: The top-level <final > whose entry ended the session, when `residency` is TA_ACTOR_DONE; TA_STATE_NONE otherwise, including an invoked child that was cancelled and an actor paused inside a microstep (ADR 0056). The active configuration stays empty after finishing: this names the outcome, it does not make the state active. Resolve it with ta_definition_state().

fields.name: allocated_bytes
fields.doc: Bytes the core currently allocates for this actor: the actor record, session storage (configuration and history), the data-model instance, sparse state, and queue capacities. Excludes memory the data-model adapter allocates itself. A measurement: it may change between releases.

ta_actor_load_params.doc: ta_actor_load() restores from `image`, or, when `image` is null, from `bytes` that ta_actor_offload() wrote in this system (TA_ERR_STALE for bytes from another system). With bytes, the root they carry is the data-model binding when `datamodel_binding` is null, and `root`, when non-null, receives a reference to it (none: absent), for the caller to release. `bytes` are only read.

fields.name: trace
fields.doc: The trace parent of what caused the load (ADR 0067), such as the message that found the actor unloaded: the LOADED record is written under it, so the load is in that message's trace. All zero: none.

ta_actor_offload_params.doc: Captures a stable named actor as bytes and unloads it in one step (ADR 0074): the bytes go into `arena`, only this system can load them, and their layout may change in any build. Values go through the actor's data model (value_encode). `root`, when given, is the data-model root to include, which ta_actor_load() hands back. TA_ERR_BUSY: the actor is inside a macrostep, has queued internal events, a pending completion or a parent. TA_ERR_UNSUPPORTED: its data model has no byte form for a value it holds. TA_ERR_INVALID: an anonymous actor. On any failure the actor is resident and unchanged.

ta_actor_resume_params.doc: `budget` is the number of microsteps this call may run (ADR 0009). `action_budget`, when not zero, is the number of units of executable content it may run before it pauses inside a microstep (ADR 0061): each action of a block, an <if > and a <foreach > included, and each <foreach > iteration. Either one reached answers TA_RUN_PAUSED, and the next call continues where this one stopped. Zero leaves pausing to `budget` alone. A pause that cannot save its position keeps running to the next unit.

fields.name: no_microstep_limit
fields.doc: True lifts the microstep limit (ADR 0075) for this call: a host sets it for an actor an operator released after TA_ERR_RUNAWAY.

ta_actor_spawn_params.doc: `trace` is what the bootstrap macrostep runs under (ADR 0067): the trace context, and the cause, the key of the step that spawned it or the host's parent span. All zero is none.

fields.name: pending_sends
fields.doc: Delayed sends to re-arm in the new session before it bootstraps (ADR 0074 section 8): records a host read from ta_actor_inspect() of an earlier session of this actor and stored with its data. Each keeps its send ID, due time, event, destination, target, data, content and trace parent; a due time already past fires on the next dispatch. The session's generated-ID counter moves past every generated ID among them. Event names must be this system's and content IDs the definition's (TA_ERR_INVALID otherwise). `target` and `data` are retained. `submitted` and `destination` of a custom processor's send are ignored: every record is armed afresh.

ta_actor_visit_params.doc:
Walks the resident actors (ADR 0062), invoked children included, handing `inspector` the same view ta_actor_inspect() gives for each. Actors are visited in increasing position order, starting at `from`. A position is an actor's slot, ta_actor_id_slot() of its ID: pass 0 to start, then the previous call's `next`, or the slot of an actor to resume at. No slot is TA_ACTOR_VISIT_END. A walk of everything is `from` 0 and `limit` 0, and may leave `next` null.

- The walk reached the end: TA_OK, and `next` is TA_ACTOR_VISIT_END. - `limit` visits answered TA_OK (0 means no limit): TA_OK, and `next` is the position after the last actor visited. - A visit answered anything else: the walk stops with that result, and `next` is that actor's position, so calling again offers it again. An inspector ends a walk early this way. - A null `params` is TA_ERR_INVALID; so is a null `visit`, with `next` set to `from`.

Between calls, and from inside a visit, the system may change. An actor resident for the whole iteration is visited exactly once; an actor destroyed before the walk reaches it is not visited; one spawned is visited only if its position is at or after the cursor. No position is visited twice in one iteration. A call costs O(actors visited + empty slots passed).

ta_address.doc: A named address that core holds (ADR 0065): one record per distinct (family, name) pair in a system, reference-counted. Two equal addresses in one system are the same handle, so pointer equality is address equality. Core interns a ta_actor_address a host supplies (spawn, find, unload, load); every named reference core stores or hands out is a handle. A handle core hands out is borrowed for the call; a host that keeps one retains it. Release every reference before destroying the system.

ta_arena_block.doc:
======================================================================== Arenas

A growable bump allocator over a ta_allocator. Adapters and hosts may use it for request- or definition-scoped storage; it performs no I/O and frees everything at reset or destroy.

ta_chart_codec_info.doc: What a codec is, for a host choosing one and a tool reporting what it did. Every field is fixed for the codec's lifetime.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: The representation this codec reads and writes: the registered media type where one exists ("application/scxml+xml"), otherwise a stable identifier of the implementer's choosing. It is also what a decode writes into a literal content's media_type.

fields.name: extensions
fields.doc: Conventional file extensions without the dot, terminated by an empty one; absent when the representation has none.

fields.name: description
fields.doc: One line, for a tool's --help.

fields.name: decode
fields.doc:
Decode `input` into a spec.

**The spec may point into `input`.** A codec is not required to copy, because a codec over a syntax tree keeps expression text as exact slices of the source, which is what lets an embedder map a compiled expression back to the construct it came from and run static checks on it before compiling. So `input` must stay valid as long as the spec does — until ta_definition_compile_spec() has copied it. Callers keep the buffer; codecs that do copy make that harmless.

A codec bounds its own input: nesting depth, document size, expansion. Reaching one of its bounds is TA_CHART_ERROR_LIMIT. The interface sets no bound of its own, so two codecs need not accept the same documents.

A literal <content > is decoded to bytes plus this codec's `info.name` as their media type. What those bytes are is the codec's rule: an XML codec serializes the content subtree with namespaces resolved as SCXML G.6 requires, rather than slicing the source, because what a recipient must see is a re-serialization and not the author's bytes.

TA_OK, TA_ERR_INVALID with `error` saying why, or TA_ERR_NOMEM. Null when this codec only writes.

fields.name: encode
fields.doc: Write `spec` in this codec's syntax. `spec->identity` is not written: identity has no chart syntax, so a round trip that must preserve an explicit one carries it beside the document and feeds it back through ta_chart_decode_params. A literal content whose media type is not this codec's own is TA_CHART_ERROR_UNREPRESENTABLE unless the codec can carry it verbatim. Null when this codec only reads.

fields.name: arena
fields.doc: The operation's arena. Everything the decode allocates lives here — the codec's own parse, the spec, and the transients in between — and nothing outlives it. Reset or destroy it once the spec is compiled.

fields.name: identity
fields.doc: No chart syntax has a form for a definition's identity, so it is supplied here or not at all; absent means the compiler fingerprints.

fields.name: arena
fields.doc: The operation's arena: the output bytes and everything the encode needed to produce them.

fields.name: construct
fields.doc: the element or production the error is about

fields.name: attribute
fields.doc: empty when it is not about one

fields.name: message
fields.doc: a fixed phrase owned by the codec

constants.name: TA_CHART_ERROR_SYNTAX
constants.doc: not well-formed in this codec's syntax

constants.name: TA_CHART_ERROR_BAD_VALUE
constants.doc: a duration, a boolean, an ID list

constants.name: TA_CHART_ERROR_LIMIT
constants.doc: a bound this codec enforces was reached

constants.name: TA_CHART_ERROR_UNREPRESENTABLE
constants.doc: encode: the spec has no form in this syntax

ta_chart_expression_printer_vtable.doc: Renders TA_EXPRESSION_HOST back to source during an encode. A spec decoded from a document carries only TA_EXPRESSION_SOURCE and needs none; a spec built from host handles is TA_CHART_ERROR_UNREPRESENTABLE without it.

ta_chart_lowering_vtable.doc: Lowers SCXML 4.10 platform-specific executable content to a <send > to a registered I/O processor, the only form core has for it (ADR 0046). `element` is the element as written. Returning TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND refuses the document, which SCXML A.2 permits. An absent adapter refuses every such element: skipping one would silently drop behaviour the author wrote.

ta_chart_position.doc:
======================================================================== Chart codecs (ADR 0053)

A codec turns bytes into a ta_scxml_spec and back. Core defines the adapter and the in-memory form and links no parser: SCXML XML, a JSON encoding and a tree-sitter grammar are all codecs, and none is in core.

Core calls a codec only from ta_definition_import() and ta_definition_encode(). An embedder may also decode and then compile with ta_definition_compile_spec() itself.

ta_chart_src_resolver_vtable.doc: Resolves <data src> and <script src> during a decode: the one route to the outside world, and the embedder's, never core's and never the codec's. For <script > the bytes are source text. TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND when `src` names nothing the resolver knows. An <invoke src> is not fetched: it is a URI the invoker interprets at run time (SCXML 6.4), and stays in the spec.

fields.name: path
fields.doc: From the spec's root to the element at fault, in the error arena. Empty when no arena was given or the error is about the whole chart.

fields.name: subject
fields.doc: The authored text at fault, borrowed from the spec exactly as given: the unknown target, the duplicate ID, the bad duration, the refused expression's source. Empty when the error is not about text.

fields.name: subject_offset
fields.doc: Within `subject`, the bytes at fault when narrower than all of it: an event descriptor's empty segment, or the range a data model reported. Both zero when all of `subject` is meant.

fields.name: related
fields.doc: A second place the error involves, borrowed from the spec: the first state with a duplicate ID, the state a target must lie within, or the existing state ID nearest to an unknown target. Empty when none.

fields.name: message
fields.doc: Why, in words: core's fixed phrase, or the data model's message copied into the error arena (empty without one).

constants.name: TA_COMPILE_ERROR_MALFORMED_SPEC
constants.doc: a tag out of range; a required pointer absent

constants.name: TA_COMPILE_ERROR_MISSING_VALUE
constants.doc: required text or expression absent or empty

constants.name: TA_COMPILE_ERROR_EXCLUSIVE_MEMBERS
constants.doc: params with content; src with content

constants.name: TA_COMPILE_ERROR_UNKNOWN_STATE
constants.doc: a target or initial names no state

constants.name: TA_COMPILE_ERROR_TARGET_OUTSIDE
constants.doc: an initial or history target outside its owner

constants.name: TA_COMPILE_ERROR_BAD_STRUCTURE
constants.doc: children, <initial > or <donedata > where the kind forbids

constants.name: TA_COMPILE_ERROR_LIMIT
constants.doc: a bound core enforces was reached

constants.name: TA_COMPILE_ERROR_EXPRESSION_REJECTED
constants.doc: the data model refused an expression

ta_compile_error_format_params.doc: Writes a compile error as one line of text, for people. The line has no stable grammar; tools read the struct. It is never longer than TA_COMPILE_ERROR_TEXT_MAX bytes, however deep the path or long the text: - a path of more than 8 steps shows its first 2 and last 6 steps, and says how many it left out; - each ID, subject, related text and message is cut at a UTF-8 boundary and ends in "..." when it is too long; - control characters are escaped everywhere, and quotes and backslashes are escaped inside the quoted subject and related text, so the line stays one line. A state step shows its ID: states[2](idle).transitions[0].targets[0]: unknown state "idel"; nearest is "idle" `spec` is the spec the error came from; it may be null, and then no IDs are shown.

ta_content_info.doc: The bytes of a definition's literal content: a <content > body or a literal send target, as the chart holds them (ADR 0053). Inspection names content by ID, as ta_delayed_send_info.target_text does.

fields.name: media_type
fields.doc: The media type the chart gave, empty when it gave none.

ta_counters.doc: Counters core keeps per definition and per system (ADR 0072). They are always on, count occurrences and never time, and move only when the step they count commits (ADR 0070), so a retry never counts twice. The system's block includes every definition that has been freed, so a sum never goes backwards.

fields.name: events_taken
fields.doc: external events that began a macrostep

fields.name: events_ignored
fields.doc: external events that enabled nothing

fields.name: internal_ignored
fields.doc: internal events that enabled nothing

fields.name: errors_execution
fields.doc: error.execution raised

fields.name: errors_communication
fields.doc: error.communication raised, in a run or not

fields.name: errors_platform
fields.doc: error.platform raised

fields.name: runs_paused
fields.doc: a budget ran out

fields.name: runs_stopped
fields.doc: an allocation failed (ADR 0070)

fields.name: macrosteps_long
fields.doc: a macrostep reached a tenth of its microstep limit (ADR 0075)

fields.name: runaways
fields.doc: a macrostep reached its microstep limit (ADR 0075)

ta_datamodel_declare_params.doc:
Named top-level data bindings (SCXML <data >). `name` is the author's data ID, borrowed for the call. declare() creates the binding with the data model's uninitialized representation; set_named() installs an initializer's value. Late binding declares every binding at bootstrap and sets each one only when its state is first entered (ADR 0032).

`bound` may be null. declare() sets `*bound` when the instance's binding already supplies a value for `name` (e.g. <param >s passed to an invoked child); the core then skips that binding's initializer.

ta_datamodel_foreach_snapshot_params.doc: <foreach >: foreach_snapshot evaluates `array` once and returns a shallow copy and its length; the core keeps the snapshot while iterating. foreach_bind assigns item `index` of the snapshot to the `item` variable and, when index_name.ptr is non-null, the index to that variable.

ta_datamodel_import_content_params.doc: Imports literal <content > or <data > content into a legal data-model value.

fields.name: roles
fields.doc: Each expression's role, by the same index (ADR 0076).

fields.name: rejected
fields.doc: Set by an adapter that returns TA_ERR_INVALID or TA_ERR_UNSUPPORTED because of one expression; `expression` stays TA_EXPR_ID_NONE otherwise. Null when the caller wants no detail.

ta_datamodel_value_encode_params.doc: Offloading an unloaded actor (ADR 0074). value_encode writes one value as bytes into `arena`; value_decode makes a value from bytes value_encode wrote, in the same process and system. What the bytes are is the data model's choice: a handle to a value it keeps alive, or the value itself. TA_OP_NOMEM means nothing changed (ADR 0070); TA_OP_ERROR means the value has no byte form. Either operation may be null: the data model then has no byte form for any value, and an actor holding one of its values does not offload.

ta_datamodel_value_text_params.doc: Conversions the SCXML `*expr` attribute forms need. value_text reads an evaluated value as text (eventexpr, typeexpr, sendidexpr, srcexpr, delayexpr, targetexpr); `*out` is borrowed from `value` and valid while it is retained, so core can parse a target URI out of it and keep the named address a send needs (ADR 0044). text_value makes a value from text, e.g. a generated send or invoke ID stored through idlocation.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: The SCXML data-model name this adapter implements, e.g. "null" or "ecmascript". Compared with ta_scxml_spec.datamodel at compile time.

fields.name: error
fields.doc: Written after every result. When the result is TA_ERR_INVALID or TA_ERR_UNSUPPORTED because of the spec, it holds the first fault in compile order (ADR 0058 section 2). Success, argument errors and TA_ERR_NOMEM leave `code` TA_COMPILE_ERROR_NONE. Borrows from `spec` and `error_arena`.

fields.name: error_arena
fields.doc: Receives the error's path and any copied message; untouched on success. Without one, `error` has no path and no data-model message.

ta_definition_encode_params.doc:
Writes a registered definition in `codec`'s syntax: ta_definition_export() followed by the codec's `encode` (ADR 0053 section 4). `identity`, when asked for, is the definition's explicit identity, which no chart syntax carries, or null when the definition was fingerprinted: feed it back as ta_definition_import()'s `identity` and the import has the same revision. A retired definition encodes until it is freed, as it exports.

TA_ERR_UNSUPPORTED when the codec cannot encode (its `encode` is null). TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND when no definition has the ID. TA_ERR_INVALID with `error` from the codec, for example TA_CHART_ERROR_UNREPRESENTABLE.

fields.name: arena
fields.doc: Holds the exported spec, the output and the codec's transients.

fields.name: identity
fields.doc: The definition's own identity, borrowed for the call.

ta_definition_event_kind.doc: The definition lifecycle, told to the host (ADR 0079). REGISTERED fires for a new registration (not a reuse by identity), including the nested children an import registers itself; RETIRED the first time a definition is retired; FREED before a registered definition's storage goes and its ID goes stale: in a cascade leaves first, and at ta_system_destroy() for every definition still alive. During every event the definition is intact: its ID resolves and `identity` is its own storage, borrowed for the call. `notify` may read definitions but must not register, retire or release one, nor spawn, destroy, resume or deliver to an actor.

ta_definition_export_params.doc:
Rebuilds the author-level spec of a registered definition (ADR 0042). Arrays and joined event names are allocated in `arena`; other text and expressions are borrowed from the definition and the system. Host expressions are the definition's retained handles, not retained again. The result stays valid until the arena is reset or the definition is freed, whichever comes first.

Export is faithful: compiling the exported spec yields the same revision as the original. `identity` is null when the definition was fingerprinted and points to the definition's explicit identity otherwise. Empty lists are exported as null, except that a handler's `actions` is never null.

TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND: no existing definition has this ID. A retired definition exports until it is freed.

ta_definition_expression_params.doc: An expression as the definition stores it: SOURCE text the compiler copied, or a HOST expression's retained value, which only the host that built it can read. Core never invents text for a host expression.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: The author's state ID, as `ta_definition_state` reports it.

ta_definition_id.doc: A registered definition: its table slot in the low 32 bits and the slot's generation in the high 32 bits (ADR 0043). Zero is never a valid ID. A freed definition's ID goes stale and never names another definition.

ta_definition_identity.doc: Process-independent identity of one exact immutable definition revision. `family` is the stable logical statechart family; `revision` is an opaque fingerprint copied/owned by the compiled definition.  Any change that can alter interpretation of a session image must produce a different revision. Given to the compiler with an empty `revision`, an identity names only the family for a chart that has no name of its own, and the revision is the compiler's fingerprint of the content (ADR 0077).

ta_definition_import_params.doc:
Decodes `input` with `codec`, compiles the spec, and registers the definition (ADR 0053 section 4). `out` is the new definition's ID.

The spec may point into `input` only until it is compiled, which happens inside this call, so `input` need only outlive the call, and `error` when it is read. `identity` is given to the codec and set on the spec: no chart syntax carries one. If registration fails, the compiled definition is destroyed here; the caller never holds an unregistered one.

TA_ERR_UNSUPPORTED when the codec cannot decode (its `decode` is null), or when the compiler refuses the spec's data model: no entry of `datamodels` has the document's `datamodel` name. TA_ERR_INVALID with `error` saying which stage refused the chart, or when `datamodels` is empty. TA_ERR_NOMEM.

fields.name: arena
fields.doc: The operation's arena: the decode, its transients, and anything `error` refers to. Core does not reset it. Reset it once the error has been read.

fields.name: datamodels
fields.doc: The data models the document may choose from, by name (ADR 0076). A document whose `datamodel` attribute names one gets the one whose `v->name` is that name; a document without the attribute gets the first. A name none of them has is refused as a compile error at the attribute, TA_COMPILE_ERROR_DATAMODEL_MISMATCH, located in `input`. At least one.

ta_definition_inspection.doc: A read-only view of one registered definition. Text and the adapter are borrowed from the system and stay valid while the definition exists (a retired definition exists until its last resident actor is gone).

fields.name: identity
fields.doc: The exact revision (ADR 0028, ADR 0038).

fields.name: document_name
fields.doc: The <scxml name> attribute, which _name reads; empty when absent.

fields.name: datamodel
fields.doc: The adapter instance the definition was compiled with. `self` identifies the instance and `v->name` the SCXML data-model name. Use it to identify the adapter; never call its operations.

fields.name: binding
fields.doc: TA_SCXML_BINDING_EARLY or TA_SCXML_BINDING_LATE, never DEFAULT.

fields.name: state_count
fields.doc: States readable with ta_definition_state().

fields.name: transition_count
fields.doc: Transitions readable with ta_definition_transition(), initial ones included.

fields.name: action_count
fields.doc: Actions readable with ta_definition_action().

fields.name: expression_count
fields.doc: Expressions readable with ta_definition_expression().

fields.name: content_count
fields.doc: Literal content readable with ta_definition_content().

fields.name: invoke_count
fields.doc: <invoke > declarations readable with ta_definition_invoke().

fields.name: retired
fields.doc: True after the definition is retired (ADR 0043).

fields.name: actor_count
fields.doc: Resident actors using this definition, unpublished replacements included.

fields.name: holds
fields.doc: Holds taken by ta_system_register_definition() and not yet released, and the definitions that nest this one (ADR 0077). The system frees the definition when both and `actor_count` are zero.

fields.name: actor_fixed_bytes
fields.doc: Bytes the core allocates for each actor of this definition before it processes events: the actor record, session storage (configuration and history), and the data-model instance. Excludes queues, the sparse state of invoked actors, and memory the data-model adapter allocates itself. A measurement: it may change between releases.

fields.name: definition_bytes
fields.doc: Bytes of the definition's own storage (its arena). A measurement.

ta_definition_nest_params.doc: Nests `child` as the chart `parent`'s <invoke > number `invoke` starts (ADR 0077): an inline <scxml > in <content >, or a literal src, compiled when the parent was defined. The parent holds the child until the parent is freed, and every invocation of that <invoke > gets the child as ta_invoke_request.definition. TA_ERR_INVALID when either definition is unknown or retired, `invoke` is out of range, or that <invoke > already nests a definition.

ta_definition_occupancy_params.doc: How many resident actors have each state active, indexed by state ID; only atomic states are ever non-zero (ADR 0072). `*count` receives the definition's state count; a smaller buffer yields TA_ERR_NOMEM.

ta_delayed_send_info.doc:
One pending delayed send owned by an actor (ADR 0054). `destination` is the resolved target for the built-in SCXML processor; custom processors receive `target`, or a literal target's text, and leave `destination` unused. `has_target_text` means the target is literal: `target` is absent, and `target_text` names the text in the owner's definition, which ta_definition_content() reads. `submitted` means the router refused the send once and it waits to be offered again (ADR 0026, ADR 0040). Everything is borrowed; retain `target` and `data` with ta_value_retain() to keep them past the synchronization window.

The same record re-arms a send when a host spawns an actor again from its stored data (ADR 0074 section 8): ta_actor_spawn_params.pending_sends.

fields.name: has_content
fields.doc: A literal <content > for a host I/O processor, by ID in the owner's definition (ADR 0053); the processor gets its bytes at dispatch.

fields.name: trace
fields.doc: The sending step (ADR 0067): the send, when it fires, names it.

constants.name: TA_DM_TEXT_EVENT_SENDID
constants.doc: _event.sendid: the author's send ID, or the generated one.

constants.name: TA_DM_TEXT_EVENT_ORIGIN
constants.doc: _event.origin, a URI that can be used as a send target.

constants.name: TA_DM_TEXT_EVENT_ORIGINTYPE
constants.doc: _event.origintype, the URI of the processor for origin.

constants.name: TA_DM_TEXT_IO_TYPE
constants.doc: _ioprocessors: the type URI of the processor at io_index.

constants.name: TA_DM_TEXT_IO_LOCATION
constants.doc: _ioprocessors: this session's location through the processor at io_index.

ta_dm_text_kind.doc:
Text of the SCXML system variables, for data models that expose them (SCXML 5.10, ADR 0068). `*out` is a view, not NUL-terminated, valid until the interpreter run that is calling the data model ends: core renders it into the run's scratch arena, or points at text it stores. Copy it before returning to core. TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND means the field has no value, e.g. no event has been processed yet, the current event has no send ID or origin, or `io_index` is past the last processor. TA_ERR_NOMEM means the arena could not grow.

`_ioprocessors` is enumerated by reading TA_DM_TEXT_IO_TYPE for io_index 0, 1, 2, ... until TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND. Index 0 is the SCXML processor.

fields.name: io_index
fields.doc: TA_DM_TEXT_IO_TYPE and TA_DM_TEXT_IO_LOCATION: the processor's registry index.

fields.name: budget
fields.doc: Must be nonzero; limits synchronous host callbacks in this call.

constants.name: TA_EXPR_ROLE_VALUE
constants.doc: evaluated for a value: expr, eventexpr, targetexpr, delayexpr, foreach array, ...

constants.name: TA_EXPR_ROLE_LOCATION
constants.doc: read and assigned: location, idlocation, a namelist or <param > location

constants.name: TA_EXPR_ROLE_SCRIPT
constants.doc: a <script > body, run for its effect

ta_expr_role.doc: How the chart uses an expression (ADR 0076): what a data model is asked to do with it at run time. A data model that compiles source text can compile each expression for its use.

ta_expression.doc: A frontend expression retained by a compiled definition. Source expressions are copied by the definition compiler. Host expressions are retained and released through their adapter; for example, a Node-API adapter retains a napi_ref rather than a callback-scoped napi_value.

ta_expression_rejection.doc:
Prepares one compiled definition for a data model. `expressions` is the definition's expression table, indexed by ta_expr_id. It is borrowed and remains valid until destroy_definition() for the same `shared` state, so the adapter may keep the pointer instead of copying. The adapter never sees the compiled definition itself.

Which expression a data model refused at prepare_definition(), and where in its source (ADR 0058). `offset` and `length` are bytes within that expression's source text; both zero when the whole expression is meant. `message` stays the adapter's: it must stay valid until core next calls the adapter, and core copies it before then.

ta_external_delivery.doc: A fully normalized event destined for another SCXML external event queue, with the trace parent the receiver's macrostep runs under: the sending macrostep's context, and the key of the step that sent it (ADR 0067). A router passes `trace` on to ta_actor_deliver().

fields.name: due
fields.doc: When the send was due (ADR 0072): the time it was sent for an immediate send, its deadline for a delayed one. A host subtracts it from its own clock to measure how late a timer fired.

fields.name: v
fields.doc: Null uninstalls the router.

constants.name: TA_EXTERNAL_EVENT_ACCEPTED
constants.doc: Delivery was accepted; an asynchronous router copied borrowed fields.

constants.name: TA_EXTERNAL_EVENT_RETRY
constants.doc: Nothing was accepted; core retains and retries the delivery.

constants.name: TA_EXTERNAL_EVENT_ERROR
constants.doc: Nothing was accepted; fault describes a communication failure.

ta_fault.doc:
invoke_id is TA_INVOKE_ID_NONE unless an invoked child generated the event.

A receiver of a fault owns its data; the message is borrowed.

fields.name: compile
fields.doc: ADR 0058

fields.name: located
fields.doc: Whether `at` says where in `input` the error is. A decode error always has a position. A compile error has one when its subject, or the nearest element above it with text, lies within `input` (ADR 0058).

ta_invoke_error.doc: An ERROR report (ADR 0081). `reason` is the event name's last token, one token of the host's choosing: not empty, with no '.' and no white space, or the report answers TA_ERR_INVALID and changes nothing. `data`, when set, is retained as the event's data. `ends` also retires the invocation, so its service's later events are ignored (SCXML 6.4.3); a lost service is reason "unavailable" with `ends`. Without `ends` the invocation stays active: its events, done.invoke. <id >, autoforwarding and cancellation behave as if no report was made. The event joins the internal queue whether the session is idle or inside a macrostep (paused by a budget, or holding a delivered event), so the report never answers TA_ERR_BUSY; an idle session starts a macrostep under the report's `trace`.

ta_invoke_info.doc: One <invoke > of a definition, by declaration index from 0 (ADR 0077): what a host needs to compile its child chart when the definition is defined. `type` is the literal type, normalized as ta_invoke_request's is ("http://www.w3.org/TR/scxml/" for the SCXML aliases and when the <invoke > names no type), or empty when the type is computed (`has_type_expr`). `content` is a literal <content > and `src` a literal src, each TA_CONTENT_ID_NONE when absent; read their bytes with ta_definition_content(). `nested` is the definition nested for it with ta_definition_nest(), or 0. TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND ends a walk over 0, 1, 2, ... and answers an unknown or stale definition.

ta_invoke_origin.doc: An event from an invoked service (ADR 0068). Core fills it: `invoker` is the registry index of the invocation's invoker, so the origin keeps its type after the invocation ends.

ta_invoke_report_kind.doc: Asynchronous outcome of a previously successful invoker start.  EVENT and DONE enter the actor's external-event flow.  ERROR appends error.communication.invoke. <id >. <reason > to the internal queue (ADR 0081).

ta_invoke_report_params.doc: `trace` is what an EVENT or DONE runs under (ADR 0067): normally the trace parent of the invoke request, so the service's events stay in the trace of the step that invoked it (napi ADR 0017 section 6). All zero is none.

ta_invoke_request.doc: One invocation to start. `type` is the resolved invoker type; the SCXML aliases "scxml" and "http://www.w3.org/TR/scxml" are normalized to "http://www.w3.org/TR/scxml/". `src` is the evaluated src/srcexpr, `data` the evaluated ` <content expr>`, and `params` the data model's aggregate of <param >/namelist values; each is empty (null vtable) when absent. A literal <content > is not imported: it arrives as `content`, the bytes the chart holds, with `content_type` its media type (empty when nothing said), and interpreting it is the invoker's business (ADR 0053, SCXML 6.4.2). Values and bytes are borrowed for the call. A service for an SCXML session spawns its child with ta_actor_spawn() and a `parent` of {parent, invoke_id}; the core then routes `#_ <invokeid >` sends, autoforwarding, and done.invoke itself. `trace` is the invoking macrostep's context and the key of the step that invoked, which such a service passes to ta_actor_spawn(), so the child's bootstrap runs under it (ADR 0067). `definition` is the definition nested for this <invoke > with ta_definition_nest() (ADR 0077), or 0: when it is set, the child is that chart, already compiled, and `content` and `src` describe where it came from.

fields.name: start
fields.doc: start must not report reentrantly through ta_actor_report_invoke().

fields.name: processor
fields.doc: The processor's registry index (ADR 0068); never 0, the SCXML processor.

ta_io_origin_class.doc: How long the URI of an event that came through an I/O processor lives, and who stores it (ADR 0068). The processor chooses the class when it builds the origin with ta_io_origin_make(): - COMPUTED: the origin holds a token, and the processor renders the URI from it with its `text` callback. Nothing is stored. For peer links, and connections whose URI follows a formula. - SCOPED: the origin names a scope (ta_io_scope_open()) that stores the URI once, for a connection or a session. After ta_io_scope_close() the origin renders empty. - MESSAGE: core stores the URI in a reference-counted entry that lives as long as any copy of the event holding it. For one request or message.

ta_io_origin_entry.doc: A stored URI of a MESSAGE origin; core owns it.

ta_io_origin_make_params.doc: Origins of events that come through an I/O processor (ADR 0068). A host builds one before it delivers the event, and puts it in the event. A MESSAGE origin comes back holding one reference, which the event then owns: ta_event_release() gives it back. An origin that never went into a delivered event is released with ta_origin_release().

fields.name: processor
fields.doc: The processor's registry index, from ta_system_register_io().

fields.name: token
fields.doc: COMPUTED: rendered by the processor's `text` callback.

fields.name: scope
fields.doc: SCOPED: an open scope of this processor.

fields.name: uri
fields.doc: MESSAGE: copied into core's storage.

ta_io_registration_params.doc: The I/O processor registry (ADR 0068). Index 0 is always the SCXML processor; registered processors get 1, 2, 3, ... in registration order. An index never changes while the system lives: registering a type again replaces its adapter at the same index. The atom returned by ta_system_scxml_io_type() is reserved.

ta_io_scope.doc: A scope of a SCOPED origin: stale once closed, never another scope's.

ta_io_scope_open_params.doc: A scope stores one URI for a connection or a session. Events refer to it without holding it: once closed, an origin naming it renders empty, so a late reply fails. Closing is idempotent for a stale scope.

ta_io_text_kind.doc: What an I/O processor renders (ADR 0068): the URI of one of its COMPUTED origins, or this session's location through it (`_ioprocessors`).

fields.name: session_id
fields.doc: The session the text is for (ADR 0066); 0 when there is none.

fields.name: address
fields.doc: Its named address, or null.

fields.name: token
fields.doc: TA_IO_TEXT_ORIGIN: the COMPUTED origin's token.

fields.name: arena
fields.doc: Where the text must be allocated.

ta_io_vtable.doc: `text` is optional. Its contract (ADR 0068): - pure: the text depends only on the processor's registration, the session and the token, for the life of the system, so a replayed history reads the same text; - it makes no calls into core: it runs while a data model evaluates an expression inside a macrostep; - all memory for the text comes from `arena`, and it keeps no pointer into it; - it answers TA_OK with the text, TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND when there is no such text (the field is then empty), or TA_ERR_NOMEM when the arena cannot grow. A processor without `text` has no location and cannot make COMPUTED origins. A Basic HTTP processor must render a location (SCXML C.2.3).

ta_log_record.doc:
======================================================================== Logging

SCXML <log > (SCXML 4.7): a label and an optional value, with an implementation-dependent rendering. The record carries the evaluated value rather than text, as ta_send does, so the host renders it with the data model it already owns (ADR 0045).

fields.name: source
fields.doc: The actor that ran the <log >.

fields.name: key
fields.doc: The step that ran it, and its trace context (ADR 0072), so a log lands next to the spans of its macrostep.

fields.name: label
fields.doc: <log label>; empty when the author wrote none.

fields.name: has_value
fields.doc: False when the <log > has no expr, or when evaluating it failed.

fields.name: value
fields.doc: Borrowed for the call; retain it to keep it (ADR 0006).

fields.name: v
fields.doc: Null uninstalls the sink; <log > then only evaluates its expression.

ta_log_sink_vtable.doc: Writing a log has no result: SCXML 4.7 requires <log > to have no effect on document interpretation, so a sink cannot fail the action.

ta_named_value.doc: One <param >: `name` is the author's parameter name, borrowed for the call.

ta_op_status.doc: What a data-model, invoker or I/O-processor operation answers. ERROR is the chart's failure: core raises the event SCXML defines for it. NOMEM says the operation could not get memory and changed nothing: core stops the run where it stands, ta_actor_resume() answers TA_ERR_NOMEM, and the operation is called again when the host resumes the actor (ADR 0047, ADR 0070). An operation that may have changed something before it ran out of memory answers ERROR.

ta_origin_text_params.doc: The text of any origin, for hosts that show or log events outside a data model. `*type` is the processor type (empty for no origin) and lives with the system. `*uri` is rendered into `arena` for actor, invoke and COMPUTED origins, and is a view of stored text for SCOPED and MESSAGE ones, valid while the origin is held and its scope is open. TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND when the origin has no text: none, or a closed scope.

fields.name: session_id
fields.doc: The session the origin was delivered to, for the processor's `text`; 0 when unknown.

constants.name: TA_ERR_RUNAWAY
constants.doc: The macrostep ran its microstep limit (ADR 0075); nothing changed.

ta_scxml_binding_kind.doc: Zero selects the SCXML default, early binding.

ta_scxml_data_spec.doc: SCXML ` <data src>` is resolved by the importer, which performs any I/O and passes the result as TA_SCXML_VALUE_CONTENT; the core performs no I/O.

ta_scxml_done_data_spec.doc: Exactly one of content or params may be present, as required by SCXML.

ta_scxml_handler_spec.doc:
One <onentry > or <onexit > handler. SCXML 3.8 and 3.9 require each handler to be a separate block of executable content: when an action fails, the rest of that handler is skipped, and the handlers after it still run. A state lists its handlers in document order.

`actions` is required, because a null `actions` terminates the handler list. An empty handler (` <onentry />`) points to an empty action list, `(const ta_scxml_action_spec[]){{0}}`, or is left out.

ta_scxml_id_kind.doc: The `id` / `idlocation` pair of <send > and <invoke >. A literal ID is the author's string; LOCATION stores the ID the processor generates each time the element executes. A zero-initialized value is absent, in which case the processor still generates an ID but does not store it.

ta_scxml_invoke_spec.doc: `type` names a registered invoker (`type` / `typeexpr`); `src` is the `src` / `srcexpr` pair; `data` is the inline <content >. SCXML `namelist` is lowered to `params` as for <send >.

ta_scxml_send_spec.doc: `type` names a registered I/O processor (`type` / `typeexpr`); absent selects the built-in SCXML Event I/O Processor. A literal `delay` is an SCXML duration such as "500ms" or "5s" and is compiled to logical milliseconds; a `delayexpr` is evaluated when the send executes. SCXML `namelist` is lowered to `params`: each name becomes a parameter whose value is a TA_SCXML_VALUE_LOCATION of the same name.

fields.name: datamodel
fields.doc: The <scxml > `datamodel` attribute: the data model this document requires. Absent means no requirement. The compiler returns TA_ERR_UNSUPPORTED when it differs from the adapter's name.

fields.name: script
fields.doc: The <scxml > <script > child (SCXML 3.2.2, 5.8), absent when zero. Each session runs it once at initialization: after early-bound data is initialized and before the initial transition is taken. A runtime failure queues error.execution. <script src> is fetched by the importer and passed as source text; the core performs no I/O.

ta_scxml_string_kind.doc: An SCXML attribute pair of the form `x` / `xexpr`: either literal text written by the author or an expression evaluated when the element executes. A zero-initialized value is absent.

fields.name: media_type
fields.doc: What these bytes are, as the codec that produced them knows it; the decoding codec's info.name. Empty when nothing said. Opaque to core.

ta_send.doc: One send to a host I/O processor. `target` is the evaluated `targetexpr`; `target_text` is a literal `target`, the text the chart wrote, which is never imported into the data model, so a chart on the null data model can name one. At most one of them is present. `data` is the evaluated ` <content expr>`, namelist or <param >s; `content` is a literal <content >, delivered as the bytes the chart holds and not imported into the data model (ADR 0053). `content_type` is the literal's media type, empty when nothing said. At most one of `data` and `content` is present. `trace` is the sending macrostep's context and the key of the step that sent it (ADR 0067), for the processor to carry, as a `traceparent` header for example. Everything is borrowed for the call.

ta_spec_member.doc:
Compile a sentinel-terminated SCXML specification into an immutable definition.

The compiler resolves state IDs and event descriptors, interns named send events, I/O processor and invoker types, and literal send and invoke IDs, validates the complete tree, and copies all data it retains. Thus the specification may be a nested compound literal with automatic storage. Every optional field is absent when zero-initialized; no field takes a runtime identifier such as `ta_expr_id`, `ta_send_id`, or `ta_atom`.

Compile errors (ADR 0058)

A refused spec is described by what is wrong (the code and message), where in the spec (a path of steps from the root), and which authored text is at fault (`subject`, the spec's own pointer, never a copy). When the spec came from a codec that keeps text as slices of its input, `subject` points into that input, which is how ta_definition_import() turns it into a line and column.

One step from a spec's root toward the element an error is about: a member of the element reached so far and, for a list member, the index in it.

ta_state_info.doc: Static facts about one state of a registered definition. `id` is the author's state ID and is borrowed from the system. `parent` is TA_STATE_NONE for top-level states. TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND ends iteration over state IDs 0, 1, 2, ... in document order; it is also the result when the definition ID is unknown or stale. A retired definition is readable until it is freed.

ta_state_kind.doc: The kind of a compiled state, as reported by ta_definition_state().

ta_step_key.doc:
Trace context and cause (ADR 0067). They travel next to an event, not in it: an SCXML event has no such field, so data models never see them, and internal queue entries do not carry them.

A step key names one step of one session: macrostep `macrostep` of session `session` (ADR 0066), and microstep `microstep` within it, where 0 is the macrostep itself. Macrosteps count from 1 per session, and 0 is outside a macrostep. The counters run whether or not a trace sink is installed, so keys are the same with tracing on or off. A cause with `session` 0 is the host's: `macrostep` holds its parent span ID, or 0 for none. A lifecycle record (SPAWNED, LOADED, UNLOADED, FINISHED, DESTROYED) is outside every macrostep: its key is (session, 0, n), where n counts the session's lifecycle records from 1 across residency, so each has its own span ID. FINISHED names the step that finished as its `cause`.

ta_system_definitions_params.doc: One page of the definitions the system holds, in slot order (ADR 0078): every registered definition not yet freed, retired ones included (ta_definition_inspect() says which). A definition ID's low 32 bits are its slot, so a walk resumes with `from` = the last ID's slot + 1, and it has ended when a page holds fewer than `limit` IDs. A definition held throughout a walk is listed exactly once. A call with too small a buffer writes what fits, answers TA_ERR_NOMEM, and sets `*count` to the IDs the page holds, so a first call with no buffer sizes it.

fields.name: from
fields.doc: The slot to start at: 0 for the first page.

fields.name: limit
fields.doc: The most IDs this page takes; 0 means no limit.

ta_time.doc: Monotonic logical time in milliseconds, supplied by the embedder.

constants.name: TA_TRACE_AT_ENTER
constants.doc: onentry, initial, history or late data of `state`

ta_trace_at.doc: Where in a macrostep a record was written.

ta_trace_context.doc:
A W3C trace context: the trace-id is `trace_id_high` then `trace_id_low`, each big-endian, and all zero means none; `flags` are the W3C trace-flags. Core copies a context to everything a step produces, reads only its sampled flag and `detail`, and creates one only when a host asks (ta_system_new_trace, ADR 0073).

`detail` is local, not W3C: it never appears in traceparent text, so it does not leave the process. TA_TRACE_DETAIL_WATCHED makes a sampled macrostep build the sink's `watched_kinds` instead of its `kinds`.

constants.name: TA_TRACE_SPAWNED
constants.doc: `cause`: the spawn's; bootstrap follows as macrostep 1

constants.name: TA_TRACE_MACROSTEP_BEGIN
constants.doc: `event`: the external event, or none; `cause`: the macrostep's

constants.name: TA_TRACE_MACROSTEP_END
constants.doc: stable, or finished; `states`: the active configuration

constants.name: TA_TRACE_ACTION_FAILED
constants.doc: `action`, `fault`; the error.execution is the RAISED record that follows

constants.name: TA_TRACE_SENT
constants.doc: `send`, `event`; its cause is this record's key

constants.name: TA_TRACE_RESUMED
constants.doc: a run continues a macrostep begun before

constants.name: TA_TRACE_STOPPED
constants.doc: an allocation failed; the run stopped where it stood (ADR 0070)

constants.name: TA_TRACE_IGNORED
constants.doc: `event`: taken, and it enabled no transition

constants.name: TA_TRACE_FORWARDED
constants.doc: `invoke`, `event`: autoforwarded to that invocation; its cause is this record's key

constants.name: TA_TRACE_LONG_MACROSTEP
constants.doc: the macrostep reached a tenth of its microstep limit

constants.name: TA_TRACE_RUNAWAY
constants.doc: the macrostep reached its microstep limit; the run stops

constants.name: TA_TRACE_DEFINITION_REGISTERED
constants.doc: Definitions (ADR 0080): lifecycle records, never sampled, written just before the definition sink hears of the same event (ADR 0079). `definition` and `identity`; the key is TA_TRACE_DEFINITIONS_SESSION, the definition ID as `macrostep`, and 1, 2 or 3 as `microstep`.

constants.name: TA_TRACE_DEFINITION_RETIRED
constants.doc: Definitions (ADR 0080): lifecycle records, never sampled, written just before the definition sink hears of the same event (ADR 0079). `definition` and `identity`; the key is TA_TRACE_DEFINITIONS_SESSION, the definition ID as `macrostep`, and 1, 2 or 3 as `microstep`.

constants.name: TA_TRACE_DEFINITION_FREED
constants.doc: Definitions (ADR 0080): lifecycle records, never sampled, written just before the definition sink hears of the same event (ADR 0079). `definition` and `identity`; the key is TA_TRACE_DEFINITIONS_SESSION, the definition ID as `macrostep`, and 1, 2 or 3 as `microstep`.

ta_trace_kind.doc:
======================================================================== Tracing (ADR 0067)

Core reports its decisions and the data they changed to one trace sink per system, as flat records. A record is written once, when the step that produced it has committed: a step that runs out of memory and runs again (ADR 0070) writes its records on the run that commits, and the step counters move only then, so an interrupted run and an uninterrupted one write the same records apart from PAUSED, RESUMED and STOPPED.

ta_trace_parent.doc: What a step inherits from what caused it: the trace context, and the key of the step that produced it. All zero is no parent.

ta_trace_position.doc: The public view of where the interpreter stands (ADR 0060, ADR 0061). IDs are the definition's compiled IDs: `action` indexes its actions, and `iteration` is the <foreach > iteration, from 0, of the innermost loop.

ta_trace_record.doc: One record. Only the fields its kind names are meaningful; the rest are zero, or NONE for IDs. Everything is borrowed for the call: retain a value to keep it (ADR 0006). `context` is the running macrostep's; `cause`, for MACROSTEP_BEGIN and SPAWNED, is the key of the step that caused it. A fault carries its `detail`, `code` and `message`. Its data went into the error.execution event of the RAISED record that follows; ACTION_FAILED also borrows it, so a sink can say why an action failed from one record. A sink never releases a record's fault data.

fields.name: identity
fields.doc: The definition's identity, for the DEFINITION_* kinds; borrowed.

ta_trace_sink.doc: Three masks of TA_TRACE_BIT(kind) (ADR 0073): core builds no record whose bit the macrostep's mask lacks. A macrostep picks its mask at MACROSTEP_BEGIN from its context: `kinds` when it has no trace ID or is sampled, `watched_kinds` when it is sampled and marked TA_TRACE_DETAIL_WATCHED, and `unsampled_kinds` when it is not sampled. Lifecycle records are outside macrosteps and never sampled: their bit is looked up in `watched_kinds` when their context is watched, else in `kinds`.

ta_trace_sink_vtable.doc: Writing a record cannot fail and cannot change the run. A sink must not call back into the system for the actor that is running; it may read the record, retain values it keeps, and inspect other actors.

ta_traceparent_parse_params.doc: W3C `traceparent` text (ADR 0073): version-traceid-parentid-flags, in lowercase hex. Parsing ignores spaces and tabs around the text, rejects version ff, an all-zero trace ID or parent ID, and anything malformed (TA_ERR_INVALID), and reads a future version by its first 55 characters. The parent ID becomes a host cause: `session` 0 and `macrostep` holding the span ID (ADR 0067). `detail` is 0.

fields.name: source
fields.doc: The state it leaves: its <transition >'s parent, or the state an initial transition belongs to; TA_STATE_NONE for BOOTSTRAP.

fields.name: type
fields.doc: EXTERNAL or INTERNAL; initial transitions are EXTERNAL.

fields.name: event
fields.doc: The event descriptor as authored; empty for an eventless or initial one.

fields.name: default_targets
fields.doc: True when the targets are SCXML's default, the first child state, and not authored. Only an initial transition can have default targets.

fields.name: condition
fields.doc: TA_EXPR_ID_NONE when unguarded; initial transitions never have a guard.

fields.name: action_count
fields.doc: The size of its block of executable content.

fields.name: document_order
fields.doc: Its place among the <transition > elements of the document; 0 for an initial transition.

constants.name: TA_TRANSITION_BOOTSTRAP
constants.doc: the document's initial transition, which bootstrap takes

ta_transition_origin.doc: Transition IDs: the <transition > elements come first, and they are the only transitions trace records name. After them come the initial transitions, one per compound state and one for the document: an <initial > element, an `initial` attribute, or SCXML's default (the first child state). The document's is the one the bootstrap takes.

ta_tree.doc: Storage for dynamically authored specification trees. A tree owns all allocations made through it until ta_tree_destroy(). Its first allocation failure is retained and reported by ta_tree_result(); subsequent writes are ignored so import code can report one result at its outer boundary.

ta_tree_list.doc: A temporary, type-erased child list owned by a ta_tree.

functions.name: ta_address_intern
functions.doc: Finds or adds the address; *out holds a new reference. Allocates only the first time a pair is seen, so only then can it fail with TA_ERR_NOMEM.

functions.name: ta_address_retain
functions.doc: Retain and release cannot fail. Release accepts null. The record is freed with its last reference.

functions.name: ta_address_view
functions.doc: The strings, valid while the caller holds a reference.

functions.name: ta_arena_allocator
functions.doc: An allocator that draws from `arena` and whose free() does nothing, so an arena can back anything that wants a ta_allocator (ADR 0053). What it allocates lives until the arena is reset or destroyed.

functions.name: ta_step_key_span_id
functions.doc: An 8-byte span ID for a step, derived the same way in every host (ADR 0067): a fixed 64-bit mix of the key, never 0. A host cause (`session` 0) returns `macrostep`, the host's own span ID, unchanged.

functions.name: ta_traceparent_format
functions.doc: Writes version 00, the context's trace ID, the span ID of the cause (ta_step_key_span_id) and the context's W3C flags, following the buffer convention (`*needed` is 56, NUL included; a too-small buffer yields TA_ERR_NOMEM). A parent with no trace ID or no cause is TA_ERR_INVALID.

functions.name: ta_trace_id_format
functions.doc: A trace ID as 32 lowercase hex digits (`*needed` is 33).

functions.name: ta_span_id_format
functions.doc: A span ID as 16 lowercase hex digits (`*needed` is 17).

functions.name: ta_trace_ratio_threshold
functions.doc: OpenTelemetry's consistent probability sampling (ADR 0073): the randomness R is the trace ID's rightmost 56 bits, the threshold is T = round((1 - ratio) * 2^56), and a trace is sampled when R >= T. The ratio is `parts` / `whole`, so every host computes the same threshold without floating point; `parts` above `whole` counts as `whole`, and a `whole` of 0 as a ratio of 0.

functions.name: ta_event_retain
functions.doc: An event owns its data, a reference to its origin's address when that is a named actor (ADR 0065), and a reference to its origin's entry when that is a MESSAGE I/O origin (ADR 0068). Retaining copies the envelope and retains all of them; it cannot fail. Releasing gives them back.

functions.name: ta_external_delivery_retain
functions.doc: Keeps a delivery past the submit call: retains its destination, its origin and its data (ADR 0050, ADR 0065). It never allocates and cannot fail. Release gives all three back.

functions.name: ta_scxml_target_parse
functions.doc:
The SCXML Event I/O Processor target URIs (ADR 0044). Core owns the grammar, so a literal `target`, an evaluated `targetexpr`, and the text core writes for `$_event.origin` agree by construction:

#_internal                 the sender's own internal queue #_parent                   the invoking parent session #_scxml_ <session >          a session by its session ID (ADR 0066) #_actor_ <family >/ <name >    a named actor by its logical address #_ <invokeid >               an invocation of the sending session

A session URI whose text is not a session ID names no session: it parses as runtime actor 0, which never exists, so a send to it is inaccessible (SCXML C.1) rather than invalid. TA_ERR_INVALID means an invalid target, which a send reports as error.execution.

A named actor target holds a reference to its interned address (ADR 0065); release the target with ta_scxml_target_release(). Interning a new address can fail with TA_ERR_NOMEM.

functions.name: ta_scxml_target_release
functions.doc: Releases a parsed target's address reference; accepts any target.

functions.name: ta_scxml_target_format
functions.doc: The URI of a target. TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND when its kind has no URI.

functions.name: ta_send_id_parse
functions.doc:
Send IDs as text (ADR 0048). A literal ` <send id>` is the author's text; a generated ID is `#_send. <n >`, the sending actor's counter. Core writes this text for `idlocation` and `_event.sendid` and reads it back for ` <cancel sendidexpr>`, so the two forms name the same send by construction: a host holding a `ta_send_id`, such as an I/O processor looking at `ta_send.send_id`, can render the text its chart holds, and a host holding that text can name the send core knows.

Parsing the generated form always succeeds, whether or not such a send exists, as a session URI does. A literal ID must already be interned in this system, since no send of it can carry text it has never seen: otherwise TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND. TA_ERR_INVALID means the text is no send ID at all, such as an empty string.

functions.name: ta_send_id_format
functions.doc: The text of a send ID, following the buffer convention: `*needed` receives the size including the terminating NUL, and a too-small buffer yields TA_ERR_NOMEM without writing, so a zero capacity is a size query. TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND when the send has no ID.

functions.name: ta_dm_host_in_state
functions.doc: Queries available to a data-model adapter while core calls into it.

functions.name: ta_dm_host_find_state
functions.doc: The state of the running definition with this author ID, for In() (ADR 0049). TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND when the chart has no such state: SCXML B.1 makes In() of it simply false, so an adapter answers that without a lookup of its own.

functions.name: ta_null_datamodel
functions.doc: The SCXML Null data model (SCXML B.1, ADR 0057), named "null". Its only expression is the In(state) predicate in a condition, with the ID quoted in ' or " or bare; In() of a state the chart does not have is false. A chart with any other expression fails to compile, and the error names the expression (ADR 0058). Every operation that needs data fails at run time as error.execution. It is stateless (`.self` is null) and allocates nothing per actor.

functions.name: ta_dm_host_state_name
functions.doc: The author's ID of a state; TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND ends iteration over 0, 1, 2, ...

functions.name: ta_origin_release
functions.doc: Releases a made origin that never went into a delivered event; accepts any origin.

functions.name: ta_null_trace_sink
functions.doc: The sink a system starts with: it wants nothing and writes nothing.

functions.name: ta_null_definition_sink
functions.doc: The sink a system starts with: it is told everything and does nothing.

functions.name: ta_actor_report_invoke
functions.doc: Externally synchronize this call; do not call it reentrantly from start.

functions.name: ta_tree_init
functions.doc: Initialize storage used while dynamically constructing a specification.

functions.name: ta_actor_prepare_replacement
functions.doc: Creates an unpublished actor and holds bootstrap effects until activation.

functions.name: ta_actor_activate_replacement
functions.doc: Atomically replaces the route, then releases held effects in SCXML order.

functions.name: ta_actor_deliver
functions.doc: Offers an external event to a resident actor: the admission test (ADR 0055). The result alone tells a host what to do with the message, so it never needs to inspect the actor first: - TA_OK: accepted; the actor holds the event, so resume it. - TA_ERR_BUSY: the actor is inside a macrostep, including one paused by ta_actor_resume()'s budgets (ADR 0061), or already holds an event. Keep the message queued for this actor. - TA_ERR_DONE: the actor has reached a top-level final state. Drop the message or route it to a dead-letter policy. - TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND: no resident actor has this ID (unknown, stale or unloaded). The receiver is gone from here; drop or route the message. - TA_ERR_INVALID: a caller error only: a null event, an event name this system never issued, or the root name. - TA_ERR_NOMEM: no memory for the event block the event would live in until its macrostep ends (ADR 0069). Keep the message and try again later; ta_system_set_event_block_cache() keeps blocks for reuse. On any result but TA_OK nothing is retained and the event is untouched. A malformed event is TA_ERR_INVALID whatever the actor's state, and a finished actor is TA_ERR_DONE, never TA_ERR_BUSY: finishing is permanent, so a host that kept a message queued would wait forever.

functions.name: ta_actor_unload
functions.doc: Evicts a named actor without terminating it. The image must be a fresh capture of actor; TA_ERR_STALE means the actor changed after capture.

functions.name: ta_actor_load
functions.doc: Restores an unloaded named actor and atomically republishes its route.

functions.name: ta_actor_reconstruct
functions.doc: Reconstructs an image under a fresh runtime ID without reading or changing the actor directory. For a named image, the logical self-address is kept; sends to that address follow the directory's current route. The image's session continues, keeping its session ID, unless a resident session holds that ID; then this is a new session (ADR 0066). ta_actor_load() always continues the session.

functions.name: ta_actor_remove_unloaded
functions.doc: Releases the name of an unloaded actor; the host then deletes its checkpoint.

functions.name: ta_actor_publish_completion
functions.doc: Retries an invoked child's completion after TA_ERR_BUSY. TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND retires it when the parent invocation was already cancelled.

functions.name: ta_actor_id_slot
functions.doc: The two halves of an actor ID, and an ID from its halves (ADR 0059). Pure: no system, no failure. A made ID is checked where it is used, like any other: a slot that holds no actor, or a generation that is not the slot's current one, is TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND there.

functions.name: ta_actor_datamodel_root
functions.doc: The data model's inspection root (its `inspect` operation). Release it with ta_value_release(). TA_ERR_UNSUPPORTED when the adapter has none.

functions.name: ta_definition_find_state
functions.doc: The state of a definition with this author ID: the inverse of ta_definition_state (ADR 0049). TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND when the definition has no such state, which is a question, not a failure.

functions.name: ta_definition_inspect
functions.doc: TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND when the ID names no existing definition: never registered, freed after retirement, or stale.

functions.name: ta_session_image_next_deadline
functions.doc: Returns TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND when the captured actor owns no delayed send.

functions.name: ta_session_image_definition
functions.doc: The registered definition an image must be restored against: the exact revision it was captured under. TA_ERR_DEFINITION_MISMATCH when only another revision of its family is registered, TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND when none is. A host uses it to build the data-model binding with that definition's data model before ta_actor_load() or ta_actor_reconstruct().

functions.name: ta_system_set_event_block_cache
functions.doc: How many empty event blocks the system keeps for reuse (ADR 0064, ADR 0069); 4 when a system is created. An actor holds a block from ta_actor_deliver() until its macrostep ends, so a host that delivers a batch of events before it resumes the actors needs a cache as large as the batch for delivery to make no allocator call. The cache takes no memory until blocks are returned to it, and it keeps only small blocks, so it holds at most `blocks` of them. A smaller setting frees the cached blocks above it.

functions.name: ta_system_set_external_event_router
functions.doc: Installs the scheduler for normalized external SCXML-session events.

functions.name: ta_system_register_definition
functions.doc: Registers a compiled definition and takes a hold on it (ADR 0077). Registration is idempotent by identity: when a registered, non-retired definition has the same identity and was compiled against the same data-model adapter, that one is the answer, it gains a hold, and `definition` is destroyed. The same identity with different content (an explicit revision reused for a changed chart) is refused with TA_ERR_DEFINITION_MISMATCH. A chart with a host expression (TA_EXPRESSION_HOST) is exempt from both: its content cannot be seen whole, so it registers beside any match. Registration takes ownership of `definition` only when it returns TA_OK.

functions.name: ta_system_find_definition
functions.doc: The registered, non-retired definition with exactly this identity; family and revision are compared bytewise. When several match, the most recently registered wins. TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND when none matches.

functions.name: ta_system_retire_definition
functions.doc: Ends a definition's availability (ADR 0043). ta_actor_spawn() and ta_actor_prepare_replacement() naming it fail with TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND, and ta_system_find_definition() skips it. Resident actors that use it keep running, and ta_definition_inspect(), ta_definition_state(), and ta_definition_export() keep working. The system frees the definition (its data-model state, its storage, and its ID) when no resident actor uses it and no definition nests it: here if none does, otherwise when the last one goes. Retiring drops every hold registration took (ADR 0077). Idempotent: retiring a retired definition, even one already freed, returns TA_OK. TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND when the ID was never issued.

functions.name: ta_system_release_definition
functions.doc: Gives back one hold taken by ta_system_register_definition(), without retiring (ADR 0077). A definition nothing holds, that no definition nests and that no resident actor uses is freed: here, or when the last of those goes. A host that registers a definition only to spawn from it or nest it releases its hold afterwards. TA_ERR_INVALID when no hold is left; TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND for an unknown or stale ID.

functions.name: ta_system_find_io
functions.doc: The registry index of a processor type; TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND when none.

functions.name: ta_system_set_log_sink
functions.doc: Installs where <log > goes; without one, a <log > only evaluates its expr.

functions.name: ta_system_set_trace_sink
functions.doc: Installs the trace sink (ADR 0067); ta_null_trace_sink() stops tracing. TA_ERR_INVALID for a sink whose `v` or `v->write` is null.

functions.name: ta_system_set_definition_sink
functions.doc: Installs the definition sink (ADR 0079); ta_null_definition_sink() stops the notifications. TA_ERR_INVALID for a sink whose `v` or `v->notify` is null.

functions.name: ta_system_set_microstep_limit
functions.doc: The microsteps one macrostep may run before ta_actor_resume() answers TA_ERR_RUNAWAY (ADR 0075), for definitions that set none of their own; 0 for no limit, the default. It applies from the next resume on.

functions.name: ta_definition_counters
functions.doc: A definition's counters; TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND for an unknown or freed one.

functions.name: ta_system_counters
functions.doc: The system's totals, freed definitions included.

functions.name: ta_system_seed_trace_ids
functions.doc: The system's trace-ID generator (ADR 0073): xoshiro256** seeded through SplitMix64. Core never reads the OS: the host seeds each system once, from random bytes in production or a fixed value in tests, and a seed gives the same sequence on every host. An unseeded system uses seed 0.

functions.name: ta_system_new_trace
functions.doc: A new trace: a random, never-zero trace ID with TA_TRACE_FLAG_RANDOM, and TA_TRACE_FLAG_SAMPLED when the system's ratio samples it. `detail` is 0.

functions.name: ta_system_new_span_id
functions.doc: A random, never-zero span ID, for a host's own spans.

functions.name: ta_system_set_trace_ratio
functions.doc: The ratio ta_system_new_trace samples at, `parts` / `whole` (see ta_trace_ratio_threshold); 1 (every trace) by default.

functions.name: ta_system_atom_text
functions.doc: The text an atom interns (ADR 0049), borrowed from the system's atom table and valid while the system is. Atoms are system-local (ADR 0007): one of another system is TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND, not undefined. This is the inverse of ta_system_intern_atom, so a host that is handed `ta_send.io_type` or `ta_invoke_request.type` can say what it was given.

functions.name: ta_system_invoke_id_text
functions.doc: The text of an invocation's ID (ADR 0049): the author's ` <invoke id>`, or the ` <stateid >. <platformid >` core generated for one without. It is what `done.invoke. <id >` names and what the `#_ <invokeid >` target spells, so a host holding `ta_active_invoke.id` can say which invocation it has. Borrowed from the system. TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND for an ID it never issued.

functions.name: ta_system_scxml_io_type
functions.doc: Returns the built-in SCXML Event I/O Processor's system-local type atom.

functions.name: ta_system_next_deadline
functions.doc: TA_ERR_NOT_FOUND means that no resident delayed send is pending.
